expressions.note: 결정을 아직 안 했지만 마음이 기울 때. lean toward도 같아요.

examples.en: I'm [leaning towards] the blue one.
My style [leans toward] minimal and clean.
We're [leaning towards] meeting in person this time.
examples.ko: 이번엔 직접 만나는 쪽으로 기울고 있어.

expressions.note: I'm not big on ~ = ~을 별로 안 좋아해.

examples.en: My family is [big on] holidays; we decorate everything.
examples.ko: 우리 가족은 명절을 엄청 챙겨서 온 집을 꾸며.

examples.en: I'm not really [big on] spicy food.
examples.ko: 나는 매운 음식을 별로 안 좋아해.

examples.en: Our company is [big on] work-life balance.

expressions.ko: (새 규정 이전부터라서) 예외로 인정받다, 기존 조건이 유지되다
expressions.note: 요금제·규칙이 바뀌어도 기존 회원은 그대로일 때.

examples.en: The price went up, but old members were [grandfathered in].
examples.ko: 가격이 올랐지만 기존 회원은 예전 조건 그대로였어.

examples.en: My phone plan was discontinued, but I'm [grandfathered in].
examples.ko: 내 요금제는 없어졌지만 나는 계속 쓸 수 있어.

examples.en: Our dog was [grandfathered in] before the no-pets rule.
examples.ko: 반려동물 금지 규정 전부터 키워서 우리 개는 예외로 인정받았어.

expressions.note: I won't name names, but... = 누군지는 말 안 할게, 근데...

examples.en: I won't [name names], but someone ate my lunch.
examples.ko: 누군지는 말 안 할게, 근데 누가 내 점심 먹었어.

examples.en: She refused to [name names] in the interview.
Without [naming names], some people never clean up.
examples.ko: 누구라고 말은 안 하겠지만, 절대 안 치우는 사람들이 있어.

expressions.note: 농담조로 작은 일에도 써요. a mini breakdown.

examples.en: I almost [had a breakdown] when my laptop died.
examples.ko: 노트북이 꺼졌을 때 거의 멘붕 왔어.

examples.en: She [had a little breakdown] before her wedding.
Don't worry, I'm not [having a breakdown]; I'm just tired.
examples.ko: 걱정 마, 무너진 거 아니고 그냥 피곤한 거야.

expressions.note: 강렬해서 잊히지 않는 장면. burnt도 가능.

examples.en: The view of the sunrise is [burned into my memory].
examples.ko: 그 일출 장면은 내 기억에 깊이 새겨져 있어.

examples.en: His shocked face is forever [burned into my memory].
examples.ko: 그의 놀란 얼굴은 영원히 잊히지 않아.

examples.en: That first concert is [burned into her memory].
examples.ko: 첫 콘서트는 그녀의 기억에 각인돼 있어.

expressions.note: be decked out in ~ = ~로 쫙 빼입다/꾸며지다.

examples.en: The whole street was [decked out] in Christmas lights.
examples.ko: 거리 전체가 크리스마스 조명으로 꾸며져 있었어.

examples.en: We [decked out] the office for Halloween.
He showed up [decked out] in a full suit.
Most of my childhood clothes were [hand-me-downs] from my cousin.
examples.ko: 어릴 때 옷은 대부분 사촌한테 물려받은 거였어.

examples.en: This desk is a [hand-me-down] from my grandpa.
I don't mind [hand-me-downs] at all.

expressions.note: be into = 빠져 있는 상태, get into = 빠지기 시작하는 순간.

examples.en: I [got into] baking during the winter.
How did you [get into] K-dramas?
My son is [getting into] soccer these days.
examples.ko: 요즘 아들이 축구에 재미 붙이기 시작했어.

examples.en: This recipe [never fails].
My grandma [never fails to] remember my birthday.
examples.ko: 할머니는 내 생일을 한 번도 잊으신 적이 없어.

examples.en: A good song [never fails to] cheer me up.
examples.ko: 좋은 노래는 언제나 기분을 좋아지게 해.

expressions.note: pull out a box(꺼내다) / pull out of a deal(빠지다).

examples.en: She [pulled out] an old photo album.
Every December, we [pull out] the Christmas decorations.
Two players [pulled out] of the tournament.

expressions.note: the glue that holds us together.

examples.en: My mom is [the glue] that holds our family together.
examples.ko: 엄마는 우리 가족을 하나로 묶어 주는 사람이야.

examples.en: She's [the glue] of our study group.
Every team needs someone to be [the glue].
examples.ko: 모든 팀엔 구심점이 될 사람이 필요해.

expressions.note: knock it out of the park, smash it도 같은 뜻.
match: knock it out of the park
knocked it out of the park

examples.en: You [killed it] on stage last night!
She's been [killing it] at her new job.
examples.ko: 그녀는 새 직장에서 엄청 잘 해내고 있어.

examples.en: Our team [knocked it out of the park] with that pitch.
examples.ko: 우리 팀이 그 발표를 완전히 성공시켰어.

expressions.note: 숫자 + 기간 + running: three years running = 3년 연속.

examples.en: She won the award three years [running].
It's rained five days [running].
I've been late two days [running].

expressions.note: ① pass on to (물려주다) ② pass away의 완곡한 표현.

examples.en: My mom [passed on] her recipes to me.
Please [pass on] my thanks to your team.
My grandfather [passed on] last spring.

roleplays.situation: 친구가 연말 모임을 어디서 할지 물어봐요.
roleplays.line: Should we meet at a restaurant or someone's place this year?
roleplays.sample: I'm leaning towards someone's place. I'm not big on loud restaurants at the end of the year.

roleplays.situation: 친구가 크리스마스 준비 다 했냐고 물어봐요.
roleplays.sample: Almost! I pulled out all our old decorations — a lot of them are hand-me-downs from my grandma — and decked out the whole living room.

roleplays.situation: 친구가 발표를 끝내고 어땠는지 물어봐요. 칭찬해 주세요.
roleplays.line: So how did I do in my presentation? Be honest.
roleplays.sample: You killed it! Your jokes never fail to wake everyone up.

roleplays.situation: 친구가 모임에서 누가 제일 중요한 역할을 하냐고 물어봐요.
roleplays.line: Who keeps your friend group together?
roleplays.sample: Jiwon is definitely the glue. I won't name names, but some of us have missed the meetup three months running.

paragraphs.text: My family is big on Christmas. Every December, we pull out the boxes of decorations and deck out the whole house. My grandmother passed on this tradition to my mom, and now my mom is passing it on to me.
I got into singing in college. Before my first performance, I almost had a breakdown backstage. But I killed it, and the sound of the audience cheering is burned into my memory.
